extracted.intended_audience: FCC licensees, tower companies, applicants for antenna licenses, State/Tribal Historic Preservation Officers (SHPOs/THPOs), the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation, and other stakeholders involved in Section 106 review of antenna collocations
extracted.subtask_description: A nationwide programmatic agreement specifying when collocation of antennas on towers, buildings, poles, and other structures is excluded from or subject to Section 106 NHPA review, including definitions, size/visibility/volume thresholds, procedural steps (notifications, SHPO concurrence, appeals), monitoring, amendments, and termination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Antenna
rubrics_metrics.description: "Antenna" means an apparatus designed for the purpose of emitting radio frequency ("RF") radiation... including the transmitting device and any on-site equipment, switches, wiring, cabling, power sources, shelters or cabinets associated with that antenna and added to a Tower, structure, or building as part of the original installation of the antenna. For purposes of this Agreement, the term Antenna does not include unintentional radiators, mobile stations, or devices authorized under Part 15 of the FCC's rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition includes both the transmitting device and on-site associated equipment/shelters/cabinets added as part of the original installation; excludes Part 15 devices, mobile stations, and unintentional radiators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Collocation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Collocation" means the mounting or installation of an antenna on an existing tower, building or structure for the purpose of transmitting and/or receiving radio frequency signals for communications purposes, whether or not there is an existing antenna on the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the universe of undertakings covered by the Agreement: mounting/installing on existing structures for communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Tower
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tower" is any structure built for the sole or primary purpose of supporting FCC-licensed antennas and their associated facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish towers from other structures (buildings, poles) for applicability of specific provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Substantial increase in the size of the tower
rubrics_metrics.description: "Substantial increase in the size of the tower" means: (1) mounting would increase existing height by more than 10%, or by the height of one additional antenna array with separation not to exceed twenty feet, whichever is greater (with limited exception to avoid interference); or (2) installation of more than the standard number of new equipment cabinets for the technology involved, not to exceed four, or more than one new equipment shelter; or (3) adding an appurtenance that would protrude from the edge of the tower more than twenty feet, or more than the width of the tower at that level (with limited exceptions); or (4) expanding the boundaries of the current tower site by more than 30 feet in any direction or involving excavation outside those expanded boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The four enumerated tests are alternate ways an addition can be "substantial"; some exceptions are allowed to avoid interference or to shelter antennas/connect via cable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — NPA applies only to collocation as defined
rubrics_metrics.description: This Nationwide Collocation Programmatic Agreement applies only to the collocation of antennas as defined in Stipulations I.A and I.B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the Agreement's scope to the collocation activity; other Section 106 responsibilities of other federal agencies are not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for towers constructed on or before March 16, 2001 (general rule and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An antenna may be mounted on an existing tower constructed on or before March 16, 2001 without such collocation being reviewed through the Section 106 process set forth in the NPA, unless: (1) the mounting will result in a substantial increase in the size of the tower; or (2) the tower has been determined by the FCC to have an adverse effect on historic properties where that effect has not been avoided or mitigated; or (3) the tower is subject of a pending environmental review or related proceeding before the FCC involving compliance with Section 106; or (4) the collocation licensee or owner has received written/electronic notification that the FCC is in receipt of a complaint from public/tribe/SHPO/Council that the collocation has an adverse effect, and that complaint is in writing and supported by substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-3/16/2001 towers are generally excluded from Section 106 review for collocations unless one of the four listed exception conditions applies; complaints must be written and supported by substantial evidence describing how the effect is adverse to qualifying attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for towers constructed after March 16, 2001 (general rule and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An antenna may be mounted on an existing tower constructed after March 16, 2001 without such collocation being reviewed through the Section 106 process set forth in the NPA, unless: (1) the Section 106 review process for the existing tower set forth in 36 CFR part 800 and any associated FCC environmental reviews have not been completed; or (2) the mounting will result in a substantial increase in the size of the tower; or (3) the tower as built or proposed has been determined by the FCC to have an adverse effect not avoided/mitigated; or (4) the collocation licensee or owner has received written/electronic notification that the FCC is in receipt of a complaint from public/tribe/SHPO/Council that the collocation has an adverse effect, with that complaint in writing and supported by substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-3/16/2001 towers are excluded only if prior Section 106/environmental reviews are complete and none of the listed exception conditions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for collocation on buildings and non-tower structures (general rule and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An antenna may be mounted on a building or non-tower structure without Section 106 review unless: (1) the building/structure is over 45 years old and the collocation does not meet criteria for collocations of small antennas (Stipulation VI); or (2) the building/structure is inside a historic district or is within 250 feet and visible from ground level and the collocation does not meet criteria for small/minimally visible antennas (Stipulation VII); or (3) the building/non-tower structure is a designated National Historic Landmark, or listed in/eligible for listing in the National Register and the collocation does not meet criteria in Stipulation VII; or (4) the collocation licensee/owner has received written/electronic notification of a complaint from public/tribe/SHPO/Council that the collocation has an adverse effect, with the complaint in writing and supported by substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age (>45 years), historic-district proximity/visibility, NHL or NR status, and supported complaints are triggers that remove the presumption of exclusion; refer to Stipulations VI and VII for specifics on small/minimally visible antenna criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior mounting exception for buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: An antenna (including associated equipment) may be mounted in the interior of a building, regardless of the building's age or location in a historic district and regardless of the antenna's size, without Section 106 review, unless: (1) the building is a designated National Historic Landmark, or listed in or eligible for listing in the National Register; or (2) the collocation licensee/owner has received written/electronic notification that the FCC is in receipt of a complaint from public/tribe/SHPO/Council that the collocation has an adverse effect, with the complaint in writing and supported by substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interior installations are broadly excluded from Section 106 review except for NHL/NR status or a supported written complaint alleging adverse effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-deployment adverse effect notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent to the collocation of an antenna, should the SHPO/THPO or Council determine that the collocation of the antenna or its associated equipment installed under the terms of the relevant Stipulation has resulted in an adverse effect on historic properties, the SHPO/THPO or Council may notify the FCC accordingly. The FCC shall comply with the requirements of Section 106 and the NPA for this particular collocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if excluded at deployment, a later determination of adverse effect by a preservation authority will trigger Section 106 compliance for that collocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional exclusion for small wireless antennas outside historic districts/non-historic properties — general triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: A small wireless antenna (including associated equipment) may be mounted on an existing building or non-tower structure or in the interior of a building regardless of the building's or structure's age without Section 106 review unless: (1) the building/structure is inside a historic district or within 250 feet and visible from ground level and the collocation does not meet Stipulation VII criteria; or (2) the building/structure is a designated National Historic Landmark; or (3) the building/structure is listed in or eligible for the National Register and the collocation does not meet Stipulation VII; or (4) the collocation licensee/owner has received a written/electronic complaint supported by substantial evidence; or (5) the antennas and associated equipment exceed specified volume limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For small wireless antennas outside historic districts and not historic properties, comply with enumerated exclusions including volume and visibility thresholds described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume limits for small wireless antennas (non-historic/non-district)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual antenna (excluding associated equipment) must fit within an enclosure no more than three cubic feet in volume, and all antennas on the structure must in aggregate fit within enclosures that total no more than six cubic feet in volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antenna volume limits are strict: 3 cu ft per antenna, 6 cu ft aggregate for the structure (including pre-existing antennas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative associated equipment volumetric limits (non-historic/non-district)
rubrics_metrics.description: All other wireless equipment associated with the structure (excluding cable runs) may not cumulatively exceed: (i) 28 cubic feet for collocations on non-pole structures that can support fewer than 3 providers; or (ii) 21 cubic feet for collocations on pole structures that can support fewer than 3 providers; or (iii) 35 cubic feet for non-pole collocations that can support at least 3 providers; or (iv) 28 cubic feet for pole collocations that can support at least 3 providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equipment volume limits vary by structure type (pole vs non-pole) and by capacity to support providers (<3 vs ≥3). Cable runs are excluded from these volumetric calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground disturbance limits and lightning rod allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth and width of any proposed ground disturbance associated with the collocation may not exceed the depth and width of any previous ground disturbance (including footings and other anchoring mechanisms). Up to four lightning grounding rods of no more than three-quarters of an inch in diameter may be installed per project regardless of the extent of previous ground disturbance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New excavations beyond previous disturbance are disallowed; limited grounding rod installations are permitted irrespective of prior disturbance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-visible equipment omission from volumetric calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: The volume of any deployed equipment that is not visible from public spaces at the ground level from 250 feet or less may be omitted from the calculation of volumetric limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equipment not visible to the public within 250 feet can be excluded when applying the equipment volumetric caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional exclusions for small or minimally visible antennas in historic districts or on historic properties (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A small antenna (including associated equipment) may be mounted on a building/non-tower structure or in the interior of a building that is (1) a historic property or (2) inside or within 250 feet of the boundary of a historic district without being reviewed through Section 106, provided specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulation VII enumerates detailed conditions (see following rubric entries) that must all be satisfied for exclusion in historic/district contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic/district exclusion — National Historic Landmark prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The property on which the equipment will be deployed is not a designated National Historic Landmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the property is an NHL, the Stipulation VII exclusion does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic/district exclusion — only antenna visible and antenna size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The antenna or antenna enclosure (excluding associated equipment) is the only equipment that is visible from the ground level (or from public spaces within the building for interior mounts), and: (a) no other antennas on the building/structure are visible from the ground level; (b) the antenna fits within an enclosure no more than three cubic feet in volume; and (c) the antenna is installed using stealth techniques that match or complement the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visibility control, small antenna size (3 cu ft), and stealth installation are required for the exclusion to apply in historic/district settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic/district exclusion — associated equipment invisibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The antenna's associated equipment is not visible from: (a) the ground level anywhere in a historic district (if located inside or within 250 feet); or (b) immediately adjacent streets or public spaces at ground level (if on a historic property not in a historic district); or (c) public spaces within the building (if mounted in the interior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated equipment must be screened/hidden from the specified public vantage points to satisfy the exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic/district exclusion — protection of historic materials and removability
rubrics_metrics.description: The facilities (including antenna(s) and associated equipment) are installed in a way that does not damage historic materials and permits removal of such facilities without damaging historic materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation must be reversible and non-damaging to historic fabric; applies equally to interior and exterior installations subject to Stipulation VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic/district exclusion — ground disturbance limits and lightning rods
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth and width of any proposed ground disturbance associated with the collocation does not exceed the depth and width of any previous ground disturbance. Up to four lightning grounding rods of no more than three-quarters of an inch in diameter may be installed per project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same ground disturbance and limited grounding rod allowances as elsewhere; protects subsurface archaeological resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic/district exclusion — complaint trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: The collocation licensee or owner must not have received written/electronic notification that the FCC is in receipt of a complaint from public/tribe/SHPO/Council that the collocation has an adverse effect. Any such complaint must be in writing and supported by substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supported written complaint alleging adverse effect negates the exclusion and triggers Section 106 review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility pole/electric transmission tower special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A small antenna may be mounted on an active-use utility pole or electric transmission tower that is a historic property or within 250 feet of a historic district without Section 106 review provided: (1) the pole/tower is not on a designated NHL; (2) the antenna (excluding equipment) fits within an enclosure no more than 3 cu ft, with cumulative 6 cu ft if multiple; (3) wireless equipment (excluding cable runs) cumulatively no more than 21 cu ft; (4) ground disturbance limits and up to four lightning rods; and (5) no supported written complaint alleging adverse effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility poles/electric transmission towers have tailored volumetric and visibility limits (notably 21 cu ft equipment cap) recognizing their functional differences from light poles/traffic structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traffic control structures / light poles — presumptive review and case-by-case exclusion procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to mount a small antenna on a traffic control structure (e.g., traffic light) or on a light pole, lamp post or other public lighting structure located inside or within 250 feet of a historic district are generally subject to Section 106 review. They may be excluded from review on a case-by-case basis if: (1) the licensee/owner has not received a supported written complaint alleging adverse effect; and (2) the structure is not historic or considered a contributing/compatible element within the historic district, following specified procedures: (a) applicant requests SHPO concurrence in writing specifying the structure and reasons; (b) SHPO has 30 days to inform applicant if it disagrees; (c) if SHPO disagrees or requests more info, applicant cannot deploy without Section 106 review; (d) if SHPO concurs or fails to respond within 30 days, applicant has no further obligations provided the collocation meets antenna/equipment/ground-disturbance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines a 30-day SHPO concurrence process and the conditions (antenna ≤3 cu ft, cumulative antenna ≤6 cu ft, equipment ≤21 cu ft, no new ground disturbance) required for exclusion if SHPO concurs or does not respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation on interior of building (historic constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: A small antenna mounted inside a building and subject to Stipulation VII is to be installed in a way that does not damage historic materials and permits removal of such facilities without damaging historic materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interior mounts within historic properties must be reversible and nondestructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacements of small wireless antennas — allowance and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An existing small antenna mounted on (historic property, inside/within 250 feet of historic district, or on/inside building over 45 years) may be replaced without Section 106 review provided: (1) the antenna being replaced has undergone Section 106 review unless such review was not required at the time of original installation or (for towers) review is not required pursuant to Stipulation III; (2) the replacement does not exceed the greater of (a) size of the existing antenna/enclosure and associated equipment being replaced; or (b) specified limits: antenna ≤3 cu ft (cumulative 6 cu ft if multiple) and wireless equipment cumulative ≤21 cu ft (excluding cable runs); (3) replacement does not damage historic materials and permits removal without damage; and (4) ground disturbance does not exceed previous disturbance (up to four lightning rods allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacements are allowed if they do not increase size/visibility beyond prior installation or stated caps and if installation is non-damaging and reversible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither execution of this Agreement, nor implementation of or compliance with any term herein shall operate in any way as a waiver by any party ... of a right to assert in any court of law any claim, argument or defense regarding the validity or interpretation of any provision of the National Historic Preservation Act or its implementing regulations contained in 36 CFR part 800.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties retain legal rights to challenge or argue statutory/regulatory interpretation despite executing or implementing the Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention by FCC licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: FCC licensees shall retain records of the placement of all licensed antennas, including collocations subject to this Nationwide Programmatic Agreement, consistent with FCC rules and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees must maintain placement records per FCC rules to support monitoring and compliance inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council forwarding of written objections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council will forward to the FCC and the relevant SHPO any written objections it receives from members of the public regarding a collocation activity or general compliance with the provisions of this Nationwide Programmatic Agreement within thirty (30) days following receipt of the written objection. The FCC will forward a copy of the written objection to the appropriate licensee or tower owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a 30-day window for the Council to forward objections and requires FCC to notify relevant licensees/tower owners of objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment channel and FCC response
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public may notify the FCC of concerns regarding application of this Programmatic Agreement within a State or with regard to review of individual undertakings. Comments shall be directed to the FCC's Federal Preservation Officer. The FCC will consider public comments and, following consultation with the SHPO, potentially affected Tribes, or the Council, as appropriate, take appropriate actions. The FCC shall notify the objector of the outcome of its actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a defined channel for public input and commits the FCC to consider and respond (after consultation) and to notify objectors of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments — proposal and concurrence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If any signatory believes that this Agreement should be amended, that signatory may at any time propose amendments, whereupon the signatories will consult to consider the amendments. This agreement may be amended only upon the written concurrence of the signatories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments require proposal, consultation among signatories, and written concurrence of signatories to take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination — grounds, notice, remedy period, and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the FCC determines, or if NCSHPO determines on behalf of its members, that it or they cannot implement the terms of this Agreement, or if the FCC, NCSHPO or the Council determines that the Programmatic Agreement is not being properly implemented or that the spirit of Section 106 is not being met, they may propose termination. The proposing party shall notify the other signatories in writing explaining reasons and afford at least thirty (30) days to consult and remedy. Parties shall consult and seek alternatives; if consultation fails to produce a reasonable alternative within the remedy period or any extension, the Programmatic Agreement shall be terminated thirty days after notice of termination is served on all parties and published in the Federal Register. Upon termination, the FCC shall advise licensees/tower owners of need to comply with applicable Section 106 requirements on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination is a structured process with written notice, minimum 30-day remedy/consultation window, publication requirement, and post-termination implementation guidance to licensees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual meeting of signatories
rubrics_metrics.description: The signatories to this Nationwide Collocation Programmatic Agreement will meet annually on or about the anniversary of the effective date of the NPA to discuss the effectiveness of this Agreement and the NPA, including any issues related to improper implementation, and to discuss any potential amendments that would improve the effectiveness of this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for routine review and communication among signatories to monitor effectiveness and consider improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and effect of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: This Programmatic Agreement for collocation shall remain in force unless the Programmatic Agreement is terminated or superseded by a comprehensive Programmatic Agreement for wireless communications antennas. Execution of this Nationwide Programmatic Agreement by the FCC, NCSHPO and the Council, and implementation of its terms, constitutes evidence that the FCC has afforded the Council an opportunity to comment ... and that the FCC has taken into account the effects of these collocations on historic properties in accordance with Section 106 and its implementing regulations, 36 CFR part 800.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies duration (until termination/supersession) and records that execution evidences FCC's consultation and consideration of effects per Section 106.
